question: Cellulitis or a skin infection directly overlying the planned aspiration site is an absolute contraindication to joint aspiration at that site.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Overlying skin infection is an absolute contraindication because the needle would carry organisms through the infected layer into the joint space. Always inspect the skin over the planned entry point before proceeding with arthrocentesis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Passing a needle through infected skin or soft tissue risks seeding bacteria directly into the joint, converting a periarticular infection into a septic arthritis. This is an absolute contraindication — choose an alternative entry site or approach if the clinical situation demands aspiration.
